Clinical details: Front-seat passenger, high-speed RTC, restrained, prolonged extrication. Seatbelt sign across chest and abdomen. GCS 13 (E3 V4 M6). BP 82/50 on arrival, major haemorrhage protocol activated. Trauma call.

Technique: Non-contrast CT head and cervical spine, followed by contrast-enhanced CT chest, abdomen and pelvis (split-bolus arterial/portal venous phase). Multiplanar bone reformats.

Head:
Thin acute left frontoparietal convexity subdural haematoma, maximum thickness 4 mm, without mass effect. No midline shift. No skull vault or skull base fracture. Grey-white differentiation preserved.

Cervical spine:
Undisplaced fracture of the C7 spinous process. No other cervical spine fracture. Alignment maintained. Craniocervical junction intact. Prevertebral soft tissues not thickened.

Chest:
Moderate right pneumothorax, maximum depth 2.5 cm at the level of the carina, with no mediastinal shift. Fractures of the right 3rd to 6th ribs anterolaterally, the 4th and 5th displaced. No flail segment. Contusion in the right lower lobe. No haemothorax. Mediastinum not widened; no mediastinal haematoma and no traumatic aortic injury. No sternal or clavicular fracture.

Abdomen:
Laceration of the right lobe of the liver involving segments VI and VII, maximum parenchymal depth 6 cm, with active extravasation of contrast on the arterial phase extending beyond the liver into the peritoneum and increasing on the portal venous phase. AAST grade IV hepatic injury. Large haemoperitoneum. Spleen, pancreas and adrenals unremarkable. Kidneys enhance symmetrically; no perinephric haematoma. No free gas. No bowel wall thickening or mesenteric haematoma to suggest bowel or mesenteric injury.

Pelvis:
Undisplaced fractures of the right superior and inferior pubic rami. Sacroiliac joints and pubic symphysis intact. Small right extraperitoneal haematoma adjacent to the fractures; no active extravasation in the pelvis. Bladder unremarkable.

Thoracolumbar spine:
No thoracolumbar spinal fracture. Alignment maintained.

Conclusion:
1. AAST grade IV liver injury with active arterial extravasation and large haemoperitoneum.
2. Moderate right pneumothorax. Right 3rd to 6th rib fractures without flail segment, and right lower lobe contusion.
3. Thin acute left convexity subdural haematoma without mass effect.
4. Undisplaced right superior and inferior pubic rami fractures with small extraperitoneal haematoma.
5. Undisplaced C7 spinous process fracture.
6. No other acute traumatic injury.

Discussed with the on-call interventional radiologist.
Preliminary findings relayed to the trauma team leader in CT at 03:15.
